summary.text: Dan LeClerc is a Democratic state representative from Hillsborough 34 who assumed office in December 2022 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A carpenter, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he recently retired from the Carpenters Union after 30 years.

paragraphs.text: Daniel LeClerc was born in New Hampshire and graduated from Manchester Memorial High School, then earned an associate degree in building construction.
His career experience includes working as a carpenter and in the construction industry, and he has served as chair of the Manchester Planning Board and as an alternate on the Amherst Planning Board.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he has been in construction for over 40 years and recently retired from the Carpenters Union after 30 years.
LeClerc assumed office in the New Hampshire House on December 7, 2022, and in the 2023-2024 session he was assigned to the Labor, Industrial and Rehabilitative Services Committee.
In the survey, he named affordability and workers' rights among his priorities, including raising the minimum wage, child care help, and limiting the shifting of state costs to property taxpayers.
He said he has been endorsed by the Carpenters Union and by unions within the Building Trades and the AFL-CIO.
